transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's the dizziness, mostly. I feel light-headed and swimmy when I stand up — getting out of bed or up from a chair. It's been troubling me.
When did you first notice it?
Oh, it's been going on for months, I think.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
It's worse first thing in the morning, and if I stand up too quickly. If I sit back down for a minute it usually settles.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
It's a swimmy sort of feeling, like I'm about to faint — not the room spinning round like some people get.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's just in my head, really — a light-headed, swimmy feeling. It doesn't spread anywhere else.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
I'd say about a 6. I nearly fell once — had to grab hold of the kitchen worktop — but I haven't actually gone over.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It comes and goes — each spell lasts less than a minute, but it happens several times a day. And now I think about it properly, I've had it about ten days, not months — I misspoke earlier.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?
No, nothing like that — no chest pain, no palpitations, no blackouts, and my arms and legs feel fine.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I've had high blood pressure for about 15 years, and I've got arthritis in both hips. That's what the tablets are for.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?

There's a new one for my blood pressure — amlodipine, 5 mg once a day — the nurse at the practice added it about two and a half weeks ago. I've taken a water tablet, bendroflumethiazide, for years, every morning. And I take paracetamol, up to three times a day, for my hip pain. There's also a small tablet I take each morning for my stomach, but I can't remember what that one's called.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
No, not that I know of. I've never had a reaction to anything.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
Well, I've stopped going to my Tuesday lunch club. I was worried about feeling faint on the bus. Otherwise I manage at home all right — I live on my own, in a ground-floor flat.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
Yes — I keep wondering if that new blood-pressure tablet is what's causing it, and whether I should stop taking it. That's really what I wanted to ask about.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
